The colour agent may treat the two as one family.

region.text: New Zealand and its first colonies, the Cook Islands and Niue

ledger.note: 1907: New Zealand becomes a Dominion. The infobox gives 'Dominion: 26 September 1907' and the text says 'King Edward VII proclaimed New Zealand a Dominion within the British Empire'; the Colony of New Zealand dated from 3 May 1841. The Cook Islands and Niue, New Zealand's 'first colonies in 1901' (realm page), are part of the Dominion.

region.text: German Samoa / Western Samoa: Upolu and Savai'i

ledger.note: 1914: New Zealand occupies German Samoa. German Samoa was captured 'shortly after the outbreak of World War I'; the expedition sailed on 15 August and landed at Apia 'two weeks later'.

region.text: German Samoa / Western Samoa: Upolu and Savai'i

ledger.note: 1920: the occupation of Samoa becomes a mandate. 'On 17 December 1920, the League of Nations formally conferred a Class C Mandate over the former German Colony of Samoa to the Dominion of New Zealand.' The Samoa Act 1921 came into force on 1 April 1922.

region.text: German Samoa / Western Samoa: Upolu and Savai'i

ledger.note: 1920: New Zealand receives the Class C mandate over Western Samoa (Upolu and Savai'i), later a UN trust territory (1946).

region.text: New Zealand's territorial claim in Antarctica

ledger.note: 1923: the Ross Dependency passes to New Zealand. The British government 'took possession of this territory in 1923' and entrusted it to New Zealand; the realm page calls it 'New Zealand's territorial claim in Antarctica' (450,000 km2 in its table). The page gives no limits and the grid has no Antarctic cells.
1925: Tokelau comes under New Zealand. 'Tokelau came under New Zealand control in 1925.' The page does not name the previous holder; the United Kingdom is the reading.

region.text: German Samoa / Western Samoa: Upolu and Savai'i

ledger.note: 1962: Western Samoa becomes independent. 'Western Samoa gained independence in 1962' (the page gives no day).

1965: the Cook Islands become self-governing. 'From 1965 the Cook Islands became self-governing'; the realm page calls the Cook Islands and Niue 'self-governing states in free association with New Zealand'. Drawn as a client (lighter tint) by reading.
1974: Niue becomes self-governing, 'as did Niue from 1974', in free association with New Zealand.

wars.name: New Zealand occupation of German Samoa
wars.outcome: German Samoa captured 'shortly after the outbreak of World War I'; New Zealand held it under occupation until the Class C mandate of 17 December 1920.
wars.note: The page names no exact date for the landing (two weeks after the sailing of 15 August) and no fighting.

certainty.note: Island coasts. The Ross Dependency (a claim) and the free-association clients (Cook Islands from 1965, Niue from 1974) are the exceptions; the dependency's limits are not on any page opened.

notes:
Written 2026-10-18 from three pages (the third beyond the 1-2 page budget, for Western Samoa). Design: the dossier is the Dominion/Realm from 26 September 1907; the Colony of New Zealand (1841-1907, with the New Zealand Wars) is left to colony-of-new-zealand, which the oc-01 batch already names and the oc-02-x batch should write; Cliopatria has no row before 1948 (its first shape is the year after the 25 November 1947 Statute of Westminster Adoption Act, which is not a territorial event and is not entered).

Not settled: the Ross Dependency limits and the Tokelau previous holder (kingdom-of-great-britain is a reading); the Kermadec (annexed 1886, a colony event), Chatham and subantarctic islands are inside Natural Earth's country and the pages give no dates; the free-association clients cook-islands and niue and the states german-samoa and samoa have no dossier and are listed for the oc-02-x batch. Cliopatria's 1948-2023 shape lacks the Chatham Islands and every dependency; the verdicts above rebuild the direct shape in steps (1907, 1920, 1925, 1948, 1962, 1965, 1974). The Pacific War produced no territorial change for New Zealand on any page opened. Wars list holds only the 1914 Samoa landing.
